mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.0% signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active whenever the rate is below its 12-month moving average.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE rises by >0.3pp, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending supply-side slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as growth expectations fall.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in this regime is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly real GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% indicates robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters with GDPC1 growth > 2.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year CPI increase above 2.5% signals rising inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy and reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a severe labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening regime, an increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals reduced liquidity, increasing equity risk premiums and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of monetary tightening periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS in this regime is below 0.04.
